problem: Sim-to-real transfer for visual navigation with RGB-based policies fails under domain shift; domain randomization lacks coverage in open-world navigation, and GAN-based domain adaptation (CycleGAN) distorts geometry and needs data from both domains.
motivation: Policies trained in simulated indoor scenes need to generalize to unseen real indoor and outdoor environments. The authors argue that a representation that is both informative for control and compact (low entropy, invariant across domains) can close the gap, and that this can be measured and explained with domain-adaptation theory.
key_idea: Feed the navigation policy a compact pre-trained representation, SEER, made of monocular depth (DPT) and a 3-class navigability map (Mask2Former semantics mapped to obstacle/ambiguous/free), so a policy trained only in indoor simulation transfers zero-shot to real indoor and outdoor scenes.
insight: Both depth and navigability are needed and they are complementary: the depth-only variant (NoSemantics) fails on open pavement (SR 0.2 in Env 3) and the navigability-only variant (NoDepth) fails on cluttered grassland (SR 0.2 in Env 4). Collapsing semantic categories to navigability strongly helps (NoNav average SR 0.42 vs 0.88). A linear-classifier estimate of the A-distance is lower in depth and navigability spaces than in RGB or GAN-transformed spaces, consistent with the generalization bound. The evidence is limited by small real-world trial counts (N=5), and the combined SEER space does not have the lowest A-distance.
method: Representation (SEER): the RGB observation is converted to depth via DPT and to a semantic mask via Mask2Former, both pre-trained and used without fine-tuning.
Navigability conversion: semantic categories are mapped to obstacle, ambiguous/unrelated or free space, which removes redundant category information and makes the representation more compact.

Control policy: an imitation-learning policy takes the representation, the current pose and the goal pose and outputs {turn left, turn right, go forward}. It is trained with cross-entropy using AdamW, lr 1e-3, batch size 200.
Data generation: 100 shortest-path expert trajectories per environment on the 72 Gibson training maps in Habitat, giving 740K samples.
Information-theoretic argument: H(Z|X) ≤ log|Z| − I(Z;Y) + H(Y), so informativeness (maximize I) and compactness (minimize H(Y)) are traded off.
A-distance analysis: domain gap in each representation space is estimated as 2(1−2·err) with a linear domain classifier, and linked to the Ben-David generalization bound.

setting.backbone: Policy network trained from scratch on frozen pre-trained DPT (depth) and Mask2Former (semantic segmentation) features
setting.training_data: 740K simulated samples (100 shortest-path expert trajectories on each of 72 Gibson maps in Habitat); the pre-trained DPT and Mask2Former are used without fine-tuning
setting.observation: monocular RGB (converted to depth and navigability), plus current pose and goal pose
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: turn left, turn right, go forward
setting.simulator: Habitat (Gibson scenes) for training; real Boston Dynamics Spot for testing
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT mesh only for training expert paths); robot localization from Spot visual odometry

numbers.bench: other:Sim-to-real local goal navigation (Habitat sim, 5 held-out Gibson maps)

numbers.eval_set_note: Lab, Corridor, Pavement, Grassland, N=5 each; Average column includes the sim environment
numbers.extra: zero-shot real, trained only in simulated indoor scenes; Average is over 5 environments
numbers.evidence: Table 1, Average: 0.88 / 0.79; Lab 1/0.92, Corridor 0.80/0.71, Pavement 1/0.94, Grassland 0.80/0.64

numbers_note: Own benchmark, not a standard one. Per-environment numbers are in Table 1; the 'Average' includes the sim env. Baselines are omitted as instructed.
results: SEER reaches an average SR of 0.88 and SPL of 0.79 across the five environments, versus CycleGAN-based adaptation at 0.65 / 0.61, the max-coverage mid-level features at 0.39 / 0.33, and RGB at 0.26 / 0.25. The gap grows with domain shift, including real outdoor scenes never seen in training.
limitations: Very small real-world sample sizes (N=5 per environment) and only a local goal-reaching task, so the statistical support is weak.
The A-distance is estimated with a linear classifier as a proxy, and the combined SEER space does not have the smallest A-distance, so the theoretical link is only suggestive.
Depends on the quality of frozen off-the-shelf depth and segmentation models and on a hand-designed category-to-navigability mapping.
builds_on: Mid-level representations for visual navigation (Sax et al.)
